rule: Keep each nc_matmul call within a 128x128 stationary tile, a 128x512 moving tile and a 128x512 PSUM output.
why: The TensorE instruction operates over a fixed-size array; larger operands must be tiled by the programmer.
trigger: Any nc_matmul whose stationary free dim >128, moving free dim >512 or partition dim >128.
fix: assert K <= nl.tile_size.pmax; assert M <= nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax; assert N <= nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax before nisa.nc_matmul(dst, stationary=lhsT_tile, moving=rhs_tile).
check_sketch: For each nc_matmul: stationary.shape[0]<=128, stationary.shape[1]<=128, moving.shape[1]<=512.

rule: Copy nc_matmul results from PSUM to SBUF with nisa.tensor_copy before issuing a dma_copy to HBM.
why: nc_matmul always writes PSUM and dma_copy only moves data between SBUF and HBM; PSUM has no DMA path.
trigger: A dma_copy whose src buffer is nl.psum.
fix: result_tmp = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf); nisa.tensor_copy(dst=result_tmp, src=result_tile_psum); nisa.dma_copy(dst=hbm_out, src=result_tmp)
check_sketch: flag dma_copy(src.buffer==psum) or dma_copy(dst.buffer==psum).

rule: Deliver the left operand already transposed as lhsT with shape [K, M] so the contraction dim K sits on the partition axis of both operands.
why: TensorE contracts over the partition dimension; nc_matmul computes stationary.T @ moving, so a non-transposed result needs the stationary operand stored transposed.
trigger: Writing a matmul of [M,K] @ [K,N].
fix: Pass lhsT=[K,M] and rhs=[K,N] tiles; result [M,N]. Transpose on the host (torch.from_numpy(lhs.T)) or with nc_transpose on device.
check_sketch: For nc_matmul(stationary, moving): stationary.shape[0]==moving.shape[0] (shared K on partition).

rule: Hoist the HBM->SBUF loads of all K tiles for a given output row/column block out of the innermost accumulation loop so they are issued once and reused.
why: Loading both tiles right before every nc_matmul serializes DMA and compute and re-loads the same tile N//TILE_N times, leaving TensorE idle between matmuls.
trigger: Profile shows gaps between matmul instructions on TensorE with DMA queues near 100% busy; dma_copy appears inside the k loop next to nc_matmul.
fix: lhsT_tiles=[dma_copy for k in range(K//128)] at the m loop; rhs_tiles at the n loop; inner loop only does nc_matmul(stationary=lhsT_tiles[k], moving=rhs_tiles[k]).
check_sketch: AST: dma_copy inside the innermost loop that also contains nc_matmul and whose source slice does not depend on the innermost index -> hoist.

rule: After hoisting, block the M and N free dimensions (several tiles per DMA) so each DMA transfer moves more bytes and fewer descriptors are issued.
why: Larger transfers amortize DMA trigger overhead and improve HBM efficiency, although each block takes longer to arrive so prefetch depth matters.
trigger: Kernel still DMA-bound after hoisting (DMA ~99% active, TensorE ~99%).
fix: TILES_IN_BLOCK_M=2, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N=2 -> BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=1024; load lhsT_tiles[bm][k], rhs_tiles[bn][k] per block, then loop bm,bn,k over nc_matmul.

rule: Block the contraction dimension K too and accumulate partial PSUM results into SBUF tiles with nisa.tensor_tensor(op=nl.add) to turn a memory-bound matmul into a compute-bound one.
why: Blocking K lets both operand blocks and the result stay resident, raising arithmetic intensity; the price is VectorE work for the SBUF accumulation.
trigger: DMA engines still active most of the kernel after blocking only M and N.
fix: TILES_IN_BLOCK_M=16, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N=2, TILES_IN_BLOCK_K=8; result_tmps memset(0) in SBUF; per block: nc_matmul over bk into a PSUM tile, then tensor_tensor(dst=result_tmps[m][bm][bn], data1=same, data2=psum_tile, op=nl.add).
source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Optimizing DMA through blocking the contraction dimension

rule: Mark the K-block loop that carries SBUF accumulation with nl.sequential_range (or plain range) rather than affine_range so the compiler does not vectorize or reorder it.
why: The tensor_tensor accumulation into result_tmps creates a true loop-carried dependency across K blocks.
trigger: Loop body reads and writes the same SBUF accumulator each iteration.
fix: for k in nl.sequential_range(NUM_BLOCK_K): ... nisa.tensor_tensor(dst=acc, data1=acc, data2=psum, op=nl.add)
check_sketch: Loop marked affine_range whose body has an SBUF tensor both read and written (not a PSUM matmul accumulate) -> warn.
source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Optimizing DMA through blocking the contraction dimension

rule: Pack several result tiles into one contiguous (TILE_M, BLOCK_N) SBUF buffer (or allocate the N-block contiguously up front) before the SBUF->HBM dma_copy.
why: One large DMA per M-tile is more efficient than many 128x512 stores; allocating result tiles as (TILE_M, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N, TILE_N) avoids even the VectorE coalescing copy.
trigger: Many small dma_copy stores from separate result tiles in the eviction loop.
fix: result_packed = nl.ndarray((TILE_M, BLOCK_N), ...); tensor_copy each bn slice; single dma_copy(dst=result[rows, BLOCK_N*n:BLOCK_N*(n+1)], src=result_packed). Better: allocate (TILE_M, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N, TILE_N) and reshape to (TILE_M, BLOCK_N).
check_sketch: Count dma_copy stores whose free size < 2KiB per partition inside eviction loop.
source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Optimizing DMA through blocking the contraction dimension; nki/guides/tutorials/matrix_multiplication.rst :: Optimization 3

rule: Split the N-block into individual M-tiles so the compiler can pipeline memset(0), matmul, tensor_tensor accumulation and SBUF->HBM eviction at M-tile granularity.
why: Finer-grained independent tiles give the scheduler overlapping stages across engines instead of one monolithic block.
trigger: Profile shows a serialized tail where accumulation/eviction waits for the whole block of matmuls.
fix: Allocate each result M-tile as (TILE_M, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N, TILE_N) and let per-tile memset/matmul/add/dma chains be independent.
source: nki/guides/tutorials/matrix_multiplication.rst :: Optimization 3: Blocking M, N and K Dimension

rule: Read a matmul in the profiler as two TensorE instructions, load-weights (stationary) and matrix-multiply (moving), and treat gaps between them as data-wait, not compute.
why: nc_matmul lowers to a weight load followed by a multiply that streams the moving operand.
trigger: Inspecting TensorE / TensorMatrix rows in Neuron Explorer.
fix: Zoom into gaps; hover the first instruction after a gap to see the semaphore it waits on.

rule: Pick kernel candidates where the profiler shows engines idle waiting on DMA in code that executes many times, and cut the graph where the region has few inputs and outputs.
why: A kernel replaces a subgraph; a minimum-cut boundary keeps the interface small while the hot region captures the idle time.
trigger: Model profile shows repeated regions with engine gaps.
fix: Use Neuron Profiler system view to find idle engines; wrap that region in a @nki.jit kernel with few tensors in/out.

rule: Profile the kernel with input sizes representative of the real workload, not the single-tile sizes used for correctness.
why: Memory-vs-compute balance and SBUF pressure only show up at realistic shapes, and the same driver doubles as a regression test.
trigger: Developing a kernel from a single-tile prototype.
fix: Grow the driver from 128x128 x 128x512 to e.g. 4096x8192 x 8192x8192 and wrap the call in profiler.profile(...) / jax.profiler.trace(...).

rule: Raise the kernel's arithmetic intensity (FLOPs per HBM byte) above the TensorE saturation threshold before tuning anything else.
why: The roofline for NeuronCore-v2 bf16 saturates TensorE at 222 Flops/Byte; a naive tiled inner loop reads 160 KB per 16 MFlops (102 Flops/Byte) and is memory bound.
trigger: TensorE utilization well below 100% while DMA queues are saturated.
fix: Reuse loaded tiles across more matmuls (hoisting, blocking) so bytes loaded from HBM per FLOP drop.
check_sketch: Estimate AI = 2*M*N*K / (bytes of HBM traffic); flag if < 222 for bf16.

rule: Count only HBM bytes when reasoning about memory-boundness; SBUF accesses are effectively free at ~20x HBM bandwidth.
why: SBUF bandwidth is high enough to sustain peak TensorE throughput, so the roofline is governed by HBM traffic.
trigger: Deciding what to cache in SBUF.
fix: Keep reused operands in SBUF and minimize dma_copy count/bytes.

rule: Accumulate the K tiles of a matmul into one PSUM tile with repeated nc_matmul calls inside an affine_range loop instead of adding partial products on VectorE.
why: TensorE can read-add-write every PSUM address; the first nc_matmul overwrites and subsequent ones accumulate, and associative reductions are not loop-carried dependencies.
trigger: Contraction dimension K > 128.
fix: psum_buf = nl.ndarray((128,512), nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum); for k in nl.affine_range(K//128): nisa.nc_matmul(psum_buf, lhsT[k], rhs[k])
check_sketch: nc_matmul into a fresh PSUM tile inside a K loop followed by tensor_tensor add -> suggest accumulation in PSUM.

rule: Size matmul blocks so arithmetic intensity exceeds the threshold while all live blocks (operands plus result accumulators) fit the SBUF budget.
why: With 16 M-tiles, 2 N-tiles and 8 K-tiles the AI is 683 Flops/Byte; lhsT needs 4 MB, rhs 2 MB and results 4*NUM_BLOCK_M MB, which fits 24 MB only while M <= 8192.
trigger: Choosing TILES_IN_BLOCK_* meta-parameters.
fix: Start from TILES_IN_BLOCK_M=16, N=2, K=8 for bf16 and shrink the M block when M > 8192 or SBUF spills appear.
check_sketch: bytes(lhsT_block)+bytes(rhs_block)+bytes(result_tiles) <= 24 MB.
source: nki/guides/tutorials/matrix_multiplication.rst :: Optimization 3: Blocking M, N and K Dimension

rule: Expect lower arithmetic intensity whenever one of M, N, K is much smaller than the others, and block all three dimensions rather than only the free ones.
why: AI = 2MNK / (2(MK+KN+MN)) for 2-byte dtypes; requiring full K resident caps the M/N block size by SBUF capacity.
trigger: Skinny matmuls or very large K.
fix: Block K and accumulate partials in SBUF (see block-k-with-sbuf-accumulation), accepting extra VectorE adds.

rule: Use nisa.nc_transpose for a partition<->free transpose and an access-pattern copy (nisa.tensor_copy or dma_copy with rearranged free indices) for a free<->free transpose.
why: Only TensorE (nc_transpose) can move data across partitions; permuting two free axes is just a different per-partition address pattern.
trigger: Any transpose request.
fix: P<->F: nisa.nc_transpose(dst, data). F1<->F2: copy in_tile[P, F1, F2] into out_tile[P, F2, F1] via strided indexing.
check_sketch: If permutation moves dim0 -> require nc_transpose; else emit tensor_copy with permuted view.

rule: Put strided or gathered access on the free dimension of SBUF/PSUM tensors; keep partition access regular and keep HBM access sequential.
why: On-chip SRAM supports flexible free-dim striding at full speed but not along partitions; HBM is fastest when read sequentially.
trigger: Even/odd split, pooling windows, 4D access patterns.
fix: in_tile[:, 0:sz_f:2] for even columns; map parallel axis to P and contraction axes to F for pooling.

rule: Lay out element-wise operands so any broadcast happens along the free dimension, which folds into the instruction for free, rather than the partition dimension, which needs a separate TensorE broadcast.
why: Free-dim broadcast is handled by the engine's access pattern; partition-dim broadcast requires nl.broadcast_to on TensorE plus a tensor_tensor.
trigger: Multiplying a [P, F] tile by a per-partition vector versus a per-free-element vector.
fix: deltaA = nisa.tensor_scalar(delta_i, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=A_i) with channels on partition instead of broadcast_to + tensor_tensor.
check_sketch: nl.broadcast_to along dim 0 feeding tensor_tensor -> suggest transposed layout with tensor_scalar.

rule: Prefer nisa.tensor_scalar over nisa.tensor_tensor when one operand is a per-partition scalar, because tensor_tensor is 2x slower for FP32.
why: tensor_tensor reads two full tiles and only runs on VectorE; tensor_scalar reads one tile plus a scalar and can run on VectorE or ScalarE.
trigger: Element-wise op where one operand has free size 1.
fix: nisa.tensor_scalar(data=x, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=vec[:,0:1]).
check_sketch: tensor_tensor whose data2 has shape (P,1) or is a broadcast -> replace.

rule: Fold a preceding multiply (and bias) into nisa.activation via its scale/bias arguments instead of issuing a separate tensor_scalar.
why: ScalarE performs a pipelined multiply-add before the non-linear function at no extra cost; this is exposed only in nisa.activation.
trigger: tensor_scalar(multiply) immediately followed by exp/other activation on the same tile.
fix: deltaA_i = nisa.activation(op=nl.exp, data=delta_i, scale=A_i)
check_sketch: Pattern tensor_scalar(mul/add) -> activation on same tensor -> fuse.

rule: Choose one partition mapping (e.g. channels on P) and keep it through all steps of a fused kernel, even if a single step would prefer otherwise, to avoid transposes.
why: A transpose between steps costs a TensorE instruction or an inefficient transposed load that outweighs a locally cheaper instruction.
trigger: Multi-step element-wise pipelines with conflicting broadcast directions.
fix: Accept p-dim broadcast + tensor_tensor for B/C in Mamba step 3/5 because delta/u already have channels on P.

rule: Define the HBM tensor layout to match the compute layout instead of using nl.load_transpose2d, which is significantly less bandwidth-efficient than a plain load.
why: Transposed DMA loads use the DMA engines poorly compared to contiguous loads.
trigger: Kernel wants seq_len on partition but HBM tensor is [channels, seq_len].
fix: Store the input as [seq_len, channels] in HBM, or keep channels on P.
check_sketch: flag nl.load_transpose2d / dma_transpose usage inside hot loops.

rule: Use the op0/op1 pair of nisa.tensor_scalar to perform two pipelined scalar ops (e.g. multiply then add) at the cost of one instruction.
why: tensor_scalar supports two operators in a pipelined fashion within one instruction.
trigger: mul followed by add with per-partition scalars.
fix: nisa.tensor_scalar(x, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=a, op1=nl.add, operand1=b)
check_sketch: Two consecutive tensor_scalar on the same tile -> merge.

rule: Implement first-order recurrences (x[t] = a[t]*x[t-1] + b[t]) with a single nisa.tensor_tensor_scan instead of a seq_len-long chain of dependent single-column instructions.
why: Each dependent tensor_scalar on a [P,1] tile pays the fixed instruction overhead; tensor_tensor_scan keeps the running state inside VectorE.
trigger: A sequential_range loop over the free dim with a loop-carried column dependency.
fix: scan = nisa.tensor_tensor_scan(deltaA, deltaBu, initial=0, op0=nl.multiply, op1=nl.add)
check_sketch: Loop over free index with body reading out[:, i] and writing out[:, i+1] -> suggest tensor_tensor_scan.

rule: When tiling the scanned dimension, carry the last column of each tile into the next tensor_tensor_scan through its initial argument and iterate the tiles with a sequential loop.
why: The recurrence creates a loop-carried dependency across free-dim tiles that affine_range would mis-specify.
trigger: seq_len tiled scan.
fix: for t in static_range(seq_len//fsz): scan=tensor_tensor_scan(a, b, initial=scan_init, ...); scan_init = scan[:, fsz-1]

rule: Accumulate partial results across a reduction loop into one SBUF buffer with += rather than materializing every partial tile.
why: A single accumulation buffer avoids allocating SBUF for all state_size partials.
trigger: Reduction over an outer loop (e.g. states) of element-wise results.
fix: scanC_accum = nl.zeros(...); for i_state in range(S): scanC_accum += scanC_i

rule: When loading one row of a tensor into a single partition, slice it as i:i+1 so the first sliced dimension (the partition dim) has size 1.
why: The first dimension with a slicing range becomes the partition dim; an integer index drops it and the next (large) dim becomes the partition dim, exceeding 128 and failing compilation.
trigger: nl.load(B[i_batch, i_state, 0:seq_len]) style loads.
fix: nl.load(B[i_batch, i_state:i_state+1, 0:seq_len])
check_sketch: Load/view whose resulting dim0 > 128 after integer indexing -> error.

rule: Find why an engine is idle by hovering the first instruction after the gap and reading the semaphore condition; a wait on a qSyncIO queue means a blocking input load.
why: Semaphore waits name the DMA queue; hovering the queue activity shows the NKI tensor being loaded.
trigger: VectorE/TensorE active percentage drops below expectation.
fix: Hoist/prefetch the named tensor's load or reorder loops.

rule: Treat profiler reload warnings while SBUF usage is only ~50% as a loop-ordering bug, not a capacity limit.
why: Reloading the same input tensors multiple times is only justified when SBUF cannot hold them.
trigger: Orange performance-warning boxes on qSyncIO rows (tensor reloaded ~7x) with SBUF usage ~50%.
fix: Reorder loops so the larger reused tensors are loaded in the outer loop (see loop-order-prioritize-largest-reuse).

rule: Order loops so that the dimension over which the largest tensors are reused is innermost (and hoist their loads above it), prioritizing reuse of the bigger operand when reuse dimensions conflict.
why: delta/u (channels x seq) are reused across states while B/C (states x seq) are reused across channels; channels (4096) dwarf state_size (16) so delta/u reuse wins.
trigger: Two input groups reused along different loop dimensions.
fix: for i_channel_tile: load delta_i,u_i; for i_state: steps 1-6  (instead of state outer, channel inner).
source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Minimizing data reloading by loop reordering

rule: Fuse sibling loops over the same index so intermediate accumulators can be declared per iteration and shrink by the trip count.
why: Pulling scanC_accum inside the fused channel loop cuts its size by n_channel_tile.
trigger: Two consecutive loops over the same range with an intermediate tensor between them.
fix: for i_channel_tile: acc=nl.zeros((128, seq_len)); ...; nl.store(..., acc)
check_sketch: Two adjacent loops with identical ranges where loop 2 only consumes loop 1 output -> fuse.
source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Minimizing data reloading by loop reordering

rule: Tile large free-dimension extents (e.g. seq_len) with an extra loop level so live tiles stay small enough to avoid SBUF fragmentation and spill/reload traffic.
why: Growing seq_len 16x without tiling increased latency 33x and dropped VectorE to 58.93% with new qSyncSpillReload/qVectorSpillReload rows; tiling seq_len at 512 recovered 94.85%.
trigger: Profile shows qSyncSpillReload0 / qVectorSpillReload0 activity and blocking waits on them.
fix: Add a seq_len tile loop (seq_len_fsize=512 to start) and carry scan state via initial=.
check_sketch: Live bytes per partition of all tiles in a loop body > ~half SBUF partition -> suggest tiling.

rule: Estimate per-partition SBUF footprint as sum(free_elems * dtype_bytes) over live tiles and keep it well under the partition capacity.
why: Three FP32 tiles of 8192 free elements consume 96 KiB per partition, half the available SBUF, which caused spilling.
trigger: Large free-dim tiles in FP32.
fix: Tile the free dim or use bf16 intermediates.
check_sketch: sum over live tiles of shape[1:]*itemsize per partition.
source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Mitigate spilling by tiling seq_len

rule: When a framework-compiled op shows sparse engine activity and very low DMA throughput at the same time, rewrite it as a fused NKI kernel.
why: Neither compute nor memory is stressed, so the op is running at low efficiency due to many small spills/reloads.
trigger: Profile: compute engines sparse, qVectorSpillReload rows dominate, DMA ~0.33% utilization.
fix: Fuse the layer in NKI with explicit tiling.

rule: Route exp/non-linear functions to ScalarE (nisa.activation), two-tensor element-wise ops to VectorE (nisa.tensor_tensor), and tensor-scalar ops to either engine to balance load.
why: tensor_tensor can only run on VectorE; activation runs on ScalarE; tensor_scalar can run on VectorE or ScalarE.
trigger: Choosing instructions for a fused element-wise pipeline where VectorE is the busiest engine.
fix: Move scalar multiplies into activation(scale=) or tensor_scalar on ScalarE when VectorE is saturated.

rule: Add explicit ordering between independent instructions by naming them (name=) and calling kernel.with_schedule([(later, earlier_or_list)]).
why: Extra dependency edges constrain the automatic scheduler without changing data flow.
trigger: Two independent instructions must run in a particular order for perf (e.g. to prioritize a critical load).
fix: nisa.reciprocal(dst=a, data=x, name='recip'); nisa.tensor_scalar(..., name='plus1'); scheduled = kernel.with_schedule([('plus1', ['recip'])])
check_sketch: Names referenced in with_schedule must exist exactly once in the specialized program.

rule: Use with nl.no_reorder(): to serialize every instruction in the block, remembering it applies to all code executed under it, including called helper functions.
why: no_reorder inserts dependency edges between every pair of instructions it dynamically encloses.
trigger: A helper function called inside a no_reorder block unexpectedly loses scheduling freedom.
fix: Keep no_reorder blocks small and avoid calling large helpers from inside them.
check_sketch: Warn when a no_reorder block encloses > N instructions or a function call.

rule: Run PyTorch scripts under NKI_SIMULATOR=1 to execute every @nki.jit kernel on the CPU simulator with no code changes; for JAX call nki.simulate(kernel)(...) explicitly.
why: NKI_SIMULATOR=1 does not currently support JAX.
trigger: Developing without Trainium hardware.
fix: NKI_SIMULATOR=1 python my_script.py   or   nki.simulate(my_kernel)(a_np, b_np)

rule: Set NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE to trn1/gen2, trn2/gen3 or trn3/gen4 explicitly; when unset the simulator auto-detects and otherwise defaults to trn3.
why: Instruction constraints and defaults differ per NeuronCore generation.
trigger: Simulating or compiling for a machine different from the current one.
fix: os.environ['NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE']='trn2'

rule: Run the simulator twice, with NKI_PRECISE_FP=0 (all low-precision stored as fp32) and the default NKI_PRECISE_FP=1 (ml_dtypes bf16/fp8), to separate algorithmic bugs from precision loss.
why: Precise mode mimics hardware rounding; disabling it removes rounding so any remaining mismatch is logic.
trigger: Simulator output deviates from a torch/numpy reference.
fix: NKI_PRECISE_FP=0 python test.py; compare; then rerun with default.

rule: Assert the simulated output contains no NaN (float) or stray 4s (int) to catch reads of memory that was never written; hardware may hide this by returning stale but plausible data.
why: The simulator fills every fresh allocation with NaN/4 sentinels that propagate through arithmetic.
trigger: Unexpected NaN in simulation output.
fix: result = nki.simulate(k)(inputs); assert not np.any(np.isnan(result)); check nl.ndarray tiles are fully written, loop bounds, conditional writes.
check_sketch: After simulate: np.isnan(out).any() -> report uninitialized read.

rule: Do not rely on the simulator to catch SBUF/PSUM capacity overflow or overlapping-address conflicts; it allocates every tensor independently.
why: The simulator's memory model has no capacity limits or aliasing, so kernels with memory conflicts pass simulation yet fail or corrupt on hardware.
trigger: Kernel passes simulation but misbehaves on device.
fix: Check footprint statically (per-partition bytes) and test on hardware; use SbufManager for deterministic layout.

rule: Restrict kernel bodies to the NKI meta-programming subset even though the simulator runs arbitrary Python; otherwise the kernel will fail at hardware compile time.
why: The simulator interprets Python directly with no compilation step, while the NKI compiler only supports a restricted subset (NKIObject classes, string-key dicts, etc.).
trigger: Kernel uses closures, arbitrary classes or dynamic control flow.
fix: Follow the NKI Language Guide value/container rules; test a hardware compile early.

rule: Never benchmark with the simulator; it models no instruction latency, engine parallelism or scheduling.
why: Kernels are interpreted eagerly and sequentially on the CPU.
trigger: Any timing of simulated runs.
fix: Profile on hardware with Neuron Explorer or run NEFFs through nrtpy.

rule: Expect nki.collectives APIs to be unimplemented in the simulator; test multi-rank collectives only on hardware.
why: Known gap in the simulator.
trigger: Kernel calls all_reduce/all_gather/collective_permute.
fix: Guard collective paths behind a flag for simulation or test on device.
check_sketch: import of nki.collectives in a kernel run under NKI_SIMULATOR=1 -> warn.

rule: Simulate LNC2 kernels by launching kernel[2]; the simulator runs two Python threads with distinct program_id over shared_hbm inputs and thread-safe sendrecv/core_barrier.
why: Inputs are wrapped as shared_hbm so both threads see the same memory.
trigger: Testing program_id-based work division without hardware.
fix: nki.simulate(kernel[2])(x)

rule: Compare simulator and hardware outputs with a loose tolerance (rtol~1e-2, atol~1e-5) because accumulation order and engine arithmetic differ.
why: Floating-point non-associativity and engine-specific implementations cause small differences even in precise mode.
trigger: Writing sim-vs-hw assertions.
fix: torch.testing.assert_close(sim_result, hw_result, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-5)
source: nki/guides/nki_simulator.rst :: nki.simulate() Explicit API; Numerical Precision

rule: Treat a clean simulator run as necessary but not sufficient; some hardware constraint checks (shape limits, dtype, buffer, engine, arch version) are still missing.
why: Hardware constraint validation is actively being developed.
trigger: Kernel passes sim, fails on HW compile/run.
fix: Report to Neuron; add explicit asserts in the kernel for tile sizes.

rule: Call a @nki.jit kernel directly inside torch_xla or jax.jit code; the tracer emits a custom-call (AwsNeuronCustomNativeKernel) that the Neuron compiler links into the surrounding NEFF.
why: The NKI compiler produces NKI IR referenced by the custom-call; the graph compiler optimizes the rest as usual.
trigger: Replacing an op in a model with a kernel.
fix: c = nki_tensor_add(a, b)  # instead of a + b; inspect with NEURON_FRAMEWORK_DEBUG=1 and XLA_SAVE_TENSORS_FILE=example1.pbtxt

rule: Wrap kernels used in training in torch.autograd.Function (forward/backward) or jax.custom_vjp (defvjp) so autodiff can call a backward kernel.
why: Custom calls have no derivative rule by default.
trigger: Kernel inserted into a training graph.
fix: class NkiAddFunc(torch.autograd.Function): forward -> nki_tensor_add(a,b); backward -> (dy, dy). JAX: @jax.custom_vjp + defvjp(f_forward, f_backward).
source: nki/guides/framework_custom_op.rst :: Using NKI in training graphs

rule: Register a kernel as a PyTorch custom op with @nki_op('lib::op', mutates_args={...}) and allocate the output with torch.empty_like before invoking the kernel with the output tensor.
why: The registration integrates with ATen dispatch; outputs passed in are HBM tensors the kernel writes.
trigger: Making a kernel callable as a regular torch op.
fix:
@nki_op('mylib::my_op', mutates_args={})
def my_op(x): out=torch.empty_like(x); my_kernel(x, out); return out

rule: Make kernel behavior depend only on its arguments (shapes, dtypes, compile-time values); global state or mutable closures can return a stale cached compilation.
why: NKI caches compiled kernels keyed on input arguments.
trigger: Kernel reads module-level variables or mutated objects.
fix: Pass configuration as explicit kwargs / NKIObject dataclasses.
check_sketch: Kernel body references free variables that are not constants -> warn.

rule: When casting during a DMA, remember the conversion goes source->FP32->destination and is unavailable for MXFP4/MXFP8.
why: DMA engines implement casting via an FP32 intermediate.
trigger: dma_copy with differing src/dst dtypes, especially integer types.
fix: Pre-quantize MX formats on compute engines; verify integer casts behave as expected.
check_sketch: dma_copy with src.dtype != dst.dtype and either is an MX dtype -> error.

rule: Expect the library QKV kernel to convert fp32 inputs to bf16 internally; pass bf16/fp16 explicitly if you need to control precision.
why: The kernel supports bf16, fp16 and fp32 but computes in bf16.
trigger: Calling nkilib qkv with fp32 hidden states.
fix: Cast hidden states to bf16 before the call.

rule: Treat in-place kernel outputs (cross_entropy_backward inplace=True, scatter_add input) as consumed: the input tensor is overwritten and cannot be reused afterwards.
why: In-place writes save HBM (num_positions x vocab x bytes) but alias the input.
trigger: Reusing logits after the backward kernel.
fix: Set inplace=False or clone before the call.

rule: Write kernels knowing that every for/if/while and Python expression is evaluated at specialization time; only nki.isa.* calls and dynamic_range loops become device operations.
why: The compiler unrolls loops, inlines calls and resolves branches, producing a flat ISA sequence; print() runs at compile time.
trigger: Large trip counts or runtime-dependent bounds.
fix: Use nl.dynamic_range(n) / register bounds for big or runtime loops; use nl.device_print for device output.
check_sketch: range() loop with trip count > threshold (e.g. thousands) -> suggest dynamic_range.
source: nki/get-started/nki-language-guide.rst :: Compilation Model; nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Scheduling options for loops

rule: Use plain range() for unrolled loops; nl.static_range, nl.sequential_range and nl.affine_range are deprecated aliases of range().
why: The newer compiler unrolls all non-dynamic loops identically.
trigger: New code or migrating tutorials that use affine_range.
fix: for i in range(n): ...
check_sketch: flag nl.affine_range/sequential_range/static_range.

rule: Load dynamic loop bounds or while conditions into a register from a 1x1 SBUF tile via nisa.register_load; register_alloc takes only an immediate int.
why: Registers are 32-bit device scalars; a tensor value must be staged in SBUF (1,1) first, and dynamic_range induction variables are frozen.
trigger: Dynamic trip count stored in HBM.
fix: cond=nl.ndarray((1,1), nl.int32, nl.sbuf); nisa.dma_copy(cond, hbm_cnt); r=nisa.register_alloc(0); nisa.register_load(r, cond); for i in nl.dynamic_range(r): ...
check_sketch: register_load src shape != (1,1) or buffer != sbuf -> error.

rule: Initialize every nl.ndarray (memset, dma_copy, or compute) before reading it; allocation does not zero memory.
why: Contents are undefined until written; HBM shared tensors used as loop conditions must be explicitly initialized too.
trigger: Accumulators or flags allocated with nl.ndarray.
fix: acc = nl.ndarray(...); nisa.memset(dst=acc, value=0.0)  or use nl.zeros.
check_sketch: Simulator NaN sentinel; static: tensor read before any write.
source: nki/get-started/nki-language-guide.rst :: Creating Tensors; nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Direct Hardware Control

rule: Allocate kernel inputs/outputs in nl.shared_hbm when launching on multiple logical cores so all cores can access them.
why: LNC2 runs the kernel on two physical cores sharing HBM.
trigger: kernel[2](...) launches.
fix: output = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
check_sketch: Kernel launched with [2] returns a tensor with buffer==nl.hbm -> warn.

rule: Keep dynamic control flow identical on every core of an LNC launch; divergent dynamic branches are undefined behavior and usually a runtime error.
why: The SDK assumes the program on each core is the same.
trigger: Using program_id to drive dynamic while/dynamic_range bounds differently per core.
fix: Divide data by program_id but keep loop structures identical.

rule: Branch on nl.num_programs() and use nl.program_id(0) to pick each core's slice so the same kernel works for LNC=1 and LNC=2.
why: num_programs returns 1 without LNC; program_id returns 0/1 under LNC2.
trigger: Writing an LNC-aware kernel.
fix: if nl.num_programs()==1: loop both halves else: i=nl.program_id(0); process input[i]

rule: Respect the three tile-size constraints: partition dim <= 128 (pmax) in SBUF/PSUM, PSUM free dim <= 512 (psum_bank_fmax), and matmul stationary free <= 128 / moving free <= 512.
why: These are hardware limits enforced by the compiler.
trigger: Any tile allocation or matmul call.
fix: Loop over math.ceil(sz_p / nl.tile_size.pmax) partition tiles using nl.ds / min() bounds.
check_sketch: Check shape[0]<=128 for sbuf/psum tensors; psum free<=512.

rule: For non-matmul (vector/scalar/gpsimd) instructions map the parallel axis to the partition dimension and the contraction axis to the free dimension.
why: Layout Constraint #2: engines reduce along the free dim per partition.
trigger: Row-wise reductions like RMSNorm or pooling.
fix: tensor_reduce over axis=free with rows on P.
check_sketch: Reduction over dim 0 of an SBUF tile -> suggest transposing layout.

rule: Assert that framework tensor shapes match the shapes the kernel tiles over; a kernel written for [128,512] fed a [256,512] tensor silently leaves the remainder as garbage.
why: Untouched rows of the output HBM tensor retain whatever was there.
trigger: Kernel hard-codes tile extents.
fix: assert in_tensor.shape == (X, Y) or loop over ceil(sz_p/128) tiles.
source: nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Tile size considerations (garbage data note)

rule: Reserve PSUM for TensorE matmul outputs and evict results to SBUF with Vector/Scalar engines as soon as possible.
why: PSUM is small; it is the accumulation target for TensorE and can be read by VectorE/ScalarE.
trigger: Allocating non-matmul intermediates in PSUM.
fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=sbuf_tile, src=psum_tile) right after the accumulation loop.
check_sketch: nl.ndarray(buffer=nl.psum) not written by nc_matmul -> warn.

rule: Keep total live on-chip data under SBUF/PSUM capacity through tiling and loop fusion; otherwise the compiler silently inserts spills/refills to HBM.
why: Memories are software-managed; overflow is handled by inserting DMA traffic that shows up as SpillReload queues.
trigger: Profile shows qSyncSpillReload / qVectorSpillReload.
fix: Reduce tile sizes, fuse loops, reuse buffers.

rule: Shape DMA transfers to cover as many partitions as possible with >= 4 KiB per partition (2 KiB minimum recommended) to approach peak bandwidth.
why: 16 DMA engines each serve 8 partitions; throughput per transfer rises with bytes per partition and saturates near 4096 free bytes.
trigger: Small per-partition transfers (e.g. [128,128] bf16 = 256 B/partition).
fix: Batch multiple tiles into one dma_copy: fp32 >= 512 elems, bf16 >= 1024, fp8 >= 2048 per partition for 2 KiB.
check_sketch: dma_copy free bytes per partition < 2048 -> warn.

rule: Spread DMA destinations across all 128 partitions; a transfer touching only 4 partitions uses a single DMA engine while 128 partitions engage all 16.
why: Each DMA engine owns 8 partition lanes.
trigger: Loading a [4,4096] tensor into 4 partitions.
fix: Reshape so rows map to 128 partitions (e.g. [128,128]) when possible.
check_sketch: dma_copy with dst partition count <= 8 -> warn single-engine.

rule: Batch data movement into fewer, larger DMA transfers; small frequent transfers are latency-bound by trigger and semaphore overhead.
why: Each transfer costs a trigger from a sequencer and a completion semaphore update from all 16 engines (even idle ones write 4 B).
trigger: Many tiny dma_copy calls in a loop.
fix: Coalesce tiles before store; load blocks instead of tiles.

rule: Budget HBM traffic against aggregate DMA bandwidth of 272 GB/s (trn1), 368 GB/s (trn2) or 528 GB/s (trn3) per NeuronCore.
why: 16 engines at 17/23/33 B/ns respectively.
trigger: Estimating memory-bound kernel time.
fix: time >= bytes / aggregate_bw.

rule: Expect DMAs in the same queue on the same engine to execute in order while different queues interleave (round robin on v2/v3, QoS on v4); choose the trigger engine via dma_copy(engine=...) only with hardware DGE.
why: Queue id is tied to the trigger engine and descriptor generation method.
trigger: A latency-critical load is stuck behind bulk transfers in the same queue.
fix: Issue critical loads from a different engine/queue; check queue id by hovering the DMA in Neuron Explorer.

rule: When building a raw .ap() pattern for SBUF/PSUM, set the partition stride equal to the storage's free-dim element count, and remember .ap() ignores any slice/offset of the view it is called on.
why: Every partition must perform the same access; .ap() addresses the underlying storage directly.
trigger: Custom strided access (every other element, etc.).
fix: u = t.ap(pattern=[(1024,128),(2,512)]) for t=(128,1024); use t.get_pattern() as a starting point.
check_sketch: ap pattern[0][0] != storage free count for sbuf/psum -> error.
source: nki/get-started/nki-language-guide.rst :: Low-level raw access pattern: ap

rule: Bound the last partition tile with min(p_end, sz_p) (or nl.ds) so inputs whose first dim is not a multiple of 128 stay in bounds.
why: Tiles must not exceed pmax, and the final tile may be partial.
fix: for p in range(math.ceil(sz_p/128)): i_p = slice(p*128, min((p+1)*128, sz_p))

rule: Use (or expect) the MLP TKG path when batch_size x sequence_length <= 96 and the CTE path otherwise; override with mode=ComputationMode.DECODE/PREFILL or force_cte_mode.
why: The library dispatches on B*S; TKG is tuned for tiny token counts (column tiling, SBUF output, FP8), CTE for throughput.
trigger: Calling nkilib mlp or designing a decode MLP.
fix: mlp(..., mode=ComputationMode.AUTO)  # TKG iff B*S <= 96
check_sketch: B*S <= 96 -> TKG features allowed.

rule: Enable store_output_in_sbuf, FP8/MX quantization, column tiling and transposed_in/out only in MLP TKG mode; they are unsupported in CTE.
why: The output is small enough to fit SBUF only when B*S is tiny; CTE handles larger inputs via HBM.
trigger: Fusing MLP output into the next layer during decode.
fix: mlp(..., store_output_in_sbuf=True, use_tkg_down_proj_column_tiling=True) with B*S<=96.
check_sketch: store_output_in_sbuf and B*S>96 -> error.

rule: Expect MLP TKG SBUF output as [BxS, H] with down-proj column tiling, or [128, H/128, BxS] (H split over partitions) without it, and size the consumer accordingly.
why: The SBUF layout follows the down-projection tiling strategy.
trigger: Chaining mlp -> next kernel in SBUF.
fix: Match the next kernel's expected SBUF input layout ([pmax, B*S, H//pmax] for attention_block_tkg X).

rule: For decode down-projection without column tiling, reinterpret W_down [I,H] as [I, lnc, 128, H/(128*lnc)] transposed to [I, lnc, H/(128*lnc), 128] so weight loads are unit-stride and the matmul initiation interval drops.
why: Unit-stride weight DMA feeds TensorE faster than strided gathers.
trigger: use_tkg_down_proj_column_tiling=False.
fix: mlp(..., use_tkg_down_proj_column_tiling=False, use_tkg_down_proj_optimized_layout=True)

rule: Use the transposed HBM layout [H0, n_prgs, H1_shard, BxS] for TKG inputs/outputs so each NeuronCore DMAs its H shard contiguously without a transpose_store.
why: Sharding H across cores with this layout removes cross-core data movement and strided stores.
trigger: LNC2 decode MLP/output-projection with H-sharding.
fix: mlp(..., transposed_in=True, transposed_out=True); output_projection_tkg(..., TRANSPOSE_OUT=True) -> [H_1=128, H_0=LNC, H_2, B*S].

rule: Expect the QKV kernel to pick TKG for short sequences and CTE for long ones, with RoPE fusion, DMA-transpose input loading and MX quantization available only in CTE and only automatic allocation in TKG.
why: The two implementations have different layouts and allocation strategies.
trigger: Requesting fused_rope on a decode-sized call.
fix: Use attention_tkg(fuse_rope=True) or attention_block_tkg for decode RoPE; use qkv(fused_rope=True) for prefill.

rule: Keep H <= 24576 and divisible by 128, fused QKV width I <= 4096, d_head == 128 for NBSd output, BSD layout for fused FP8 KV-cache quantization, and provide block_size + slot_mapping for block KV.
why: Library kernel validation limits.
trigger: Calling nkilib qkv.
fix: qkv(input[B,S,H], W[H,I], output_layout=QKVOutputLayout.BSD, ...)

rule: Write the K cache in transposed (head_dim, seq/block) layout at prefill time so decode attention can load K with d_head on partitions without an nc_transpose.
why: QK^T contracts over d_head, so d on partition is the native matmul layout; attention_tkg exposes tp_k_prior and attention_segmented_cte k_pre_transposed for this.
trigger: Designing the KV-cache layout for a decode path.
fix: qkv(..., transpose_k_cache=True); attention_tkg(cfg.tp_k_prior=True) with k_prior [B,1,d,s_prior].
source: nki/library/api/qkv.rst :: transpose_k_cache; nki/library/api/attention-tkg.rst :: K_prior Transpose Handling; nki/library/api/attention-segmented-cte.rst

rule: Fuse the residual stream into the next projection (input + mlp_prev + attention_prev) instead of a separate add kernel.
why: qkv's fused_residual_add consumes both previous outputs during its input load.
trigger: Transformer layer with residual connections.
fix: qkv(..., fused_residual_add=True, mlp_prev=..., attention_prev=...)

rule: Use attention_tkg for decode with s_active <= 7 and d_head <= 128, and attention_cte for prefill with sequence length > 256.
why: attention_tkg is tuned for tiny active sequences against large KV caches; attention_cte for long Q/K sequences with flash-style sectioning.
trigger: Choosing the library attention kernel.
fix: attention_tkg(q,k_active,v_active,k_prior,v_prior,mask,out,cfg,sbm) or attention_cte(q,k,v,...)
check_sketch: s_active<=7 -> tkg; seqlen>256 -> cte.

rule: For LNC2 decode attention shard on batch when batch is even AND (s_prior < 256 OR b*q_head*s_active > 128); otherwise shard the prior sequence (requires s_prior >= 256).
why: Batch sharding needs no cross-core reduction; sequence sharding splits the KV cache and merges softmax partials via GPSIMD SBUF-to-SBUF transfers.
trigger: attention_tkg under kernel[2].
fix: Set bs/q_head/s_active/curr_sprior in AttnTKGConfig; keep use_gpsimd_sb2sb=True.
check_sketch: if bs%2==0 and (s_prior<256 or bs*q_head*s_active>128): batch-shard else seq-shard.

rule: Feed attention_tkg with d_head on the partition axis: q [d, B*H*s_active] and k_active [d, B*s_active] in SBUF (qk_in_sb), v_active [B,1,s_active,d], out [d, B*H*s_active] in SBUF or [B,H,d,s_active] in HBM.
why: QK^T contracts over d so Q and K must have d on partitions; the output keeps d on partitions for the following output projection ([D,B,N,S]).
trigger: Wiring QKV -> attention -> output projection in decode.
fix: cfg.qk_in_sb=True; cfg.out_in_sb=True; output_projection_tkg(attention=[D,B,N,S] in SBUF, OUT_IN_SB=True)

rule: Set cfg.qk_in_sb=True whenever fused RoPE is skipped or a block KV cache is used; in-kernel mask generation (use_pos_id) is incompatible with batch sharding and block KV.
why: Library constraints of attention_tkg.
trigger: Configuring AttnTKGConfig.
fix: AttnTKGConfig(qk_in_sb=True, block_len=..., use_pos_id=False)
check_sketch: block_len>0 and not qk_in_sb -> error; use_pos_id and (batch-shard or block_len) -> error.

rule: Keep strided_mm1=True so the first matmul reads K with a strided pattern and the second matmul can stream V sequentially for better DMA throughput.
why: Trades MM1 access regularity for sequential V reads in MM2.
trigger: Decode attention over large KV cache.
fix: AttnTKGConfig(strided_mm1=True)

rule: Generate the attention mask in-kernel from position ids (use_pos_id=True) to avoid loading a [s_prior, B, H, s_active] mask from HBM.
why: Reduces memory bandwidth at the cost of requiring position IDs.
trigger: Decode attention where mask DMA is noticeable.
fix: AttnTKGConfig(use_pos_id=True), pass rope_pos_ids/start_pos_ids.

rule: Use attention_block_tkg only when batch * S_tkg * q_heads <= 128, H is a multiple of 128, d_head is even and the target is NeuronCore v3+.
why: The fused block keeps QKV, Q, K, V, scores and attention output in SBUF on one partition tile.
trigger: Fused decode attention block.
fix: attention_block_tkg(X[B,S_tkg,H] or SBUF [pmax, B*S_tkg, H//pmax], ..., out_in_sb=True)
check_sketch: B*S_tkg*q_heads<=128 and H%128==0 and d_head%2==0.

rule: Fuse pre-norm, QKV, RoPE, QK-norm, attention, KV-cache update and output projection in one kernel so only X, weights, caches and the final output touch HBM.
why: Decode is HBM-bandwidth bound; eliminating intermediate round-trips is the main lever.
trigger: Building a decode layer.
fix: Use attention_block_tkg or compose attention_tkg(out_in_sb) -> output_projection_tkg(OUT_IN_SB) with a shared SbufManager.

rule: Update the KV cache with one batched vector-offset DMA for S_tkg=1 and per-batch scalar-offset DMAs for S_tkg>1; block caches use indirect addressing via block slot indices.
why: Vector offsets let a single DMA scatter all batches' tokens; scalar offsets are needed when each batch writes a range.
trigger: Writing new K/V tokens into the cache.
fix: For S_tkg==1: dma with vector_offset=kv_cache_update_idx; else loop over batch with scalar_offset.

rule: Provide RoPE cos/sin as [d_head//2, B, S] with the half-head dimension on partitions for decode kernels, and prefer the contiguous (first half, second half) head layout over interleaved.
why: RoPE rotates pairs across the two halves; with d on partitions each half maps to a partition range so cos/sin broadcast along free dims.
trigger: attention_block_tkg / RoPE / transformer_tkg inputs.
fix: cos=[d_head//2, B, S_tkg]; rope_contiguous_layout=True

rule: Convert interleaved RoPE layout to contiguous with a permutation-matrix matmul in SBUF only when B*n_heads*S <= 512 (gemm_moving_fmax); otherwise use strided DMA with step=2.
why: The SBUF matmul path needs the whole free extent in one moving tile; strided DMA works for any size.
trigger: Model weights use interleaved (even/odd) RoPE.
fix: RoPE(x, cos, sin, contiguous_layout=False, relayout_in_sbuf=(B*n_heads*S<=512))
check_sketch: relayout_in_sbuf and B*n_heads*S>512 -> error.

rule: Use the standalone RoPE kernel with x [d_head, B, n_heads, S], d_head in {64,128}, B <= 64, S <= 512, n_heads <= 16, and S divisible by the program count when lnc_shard=True; use RoPE_sbuf for in-SBUF fusion.
why: Validated ranges of the library kernel; LNC sharding tiles the sequence dimension.
trigger: Calling nkilib RoPE.
fix: RoPE(x_in, cos, sin, lnc_shard=True)  # S % n_prgs == 0

rule: For output_projection_tkg keep B*S <= 128, D <= 128, H divisible by LNC and by 512*LNC (or 128*LNC with TRANSPOSE_OUT), and N*H <= 81920 (fp32) / 163840 (16-bit) when TRANSPOSE_OUT.
why: LNC shards the weight hidden dimension so each core writes its own H slice without collectives.
trigger: Decode output projection.
fix: output_projection_tkg(attention[D,B,N,S], weight[N*D,H], OUT_IN_SB=True)
check_sketch: B*S<=128; H%(512*LNC)==0 or (TRANSPOSE_OUT and H%(128*LNC)==0).

rule: In decode, place the heads dimension next to the (tiny) sequence dimension ([D,B,N,S]) so GQA loads several heads in one DMA; CTE uses [B,N,D,S] instead.
why: With S small, N adjacent to S makes a contiguous free extent for multi-head loads.
trigger: Choosing attention output layout for TKG vs CTE.
fix: TKG: attention[d,b,n,s]; CTE: attention[b,n,d,s].

rule: Load projection weights in blocks (several tiles per DMA) to encourage prefetching ahead of the matmuls.
why: Decode projections are weight-bandwidth bound; block loads keep DMA queues full.
trigger: Weight streaming in TKG kernels.
fix: Follow output_projection_tkg's block-based weight loading.

rule: Fold the heads dimension N into D for the output-projection contraction (N*D on partitions, up to 128 at a time) when beneficial.
why: A larger contraction tile uses the full TensorE array instead of many d-wide matmuls.
trigger: d_head < 128 (e.g. 64) with several heads.
fix: Treat weight as [N*D, H] and stack heads on partitions.

rule: Use output_projection_cte with S >= 512 (smaller S degrades), attention [B,N,D,S], D <= 128, H <= 32768 (validated 20705), H divisible by LNC; fp32 may not fit SBUF.
why: Validated limits and layout contract shared with other CTE kernels to avoid transposes.
trigger: Prefill output projection.
fix: output_projection_cte(attention[B,N,D,S], weight[N*D,H])

rule: Alternate tensor_copy evictions between ScalarE and VectorE to balance engine load.
why: Both engines can read PSUM/SBUF; spreading copies avoids one engine becoming the bottleneck.
trigger: Many PSUM->SBUF evictions in a matmul-heavy kernel.
fix: Alternate engine= on nisa.tensor_copy per tile.

rule: Broadcast a [1,H] bias across partitions with stream_shuffle_broadcast (DVE) by default, or with a TensorE ones-matmul when TensorE is idle.
why: Partition broadcast needs a hardware shuffle or a matmul; the library offers both (use_PE_broadcast_w_bias / use_pe_broadcast).
trigger: Adding bias/gamma rows to a [128, H] tile.
fix: nkilib stream_shuffle_broadcast(bias) or matmul(ones[1,128].T, bias[1,H]).
source: nki/library/api/output-projection-cte.rst :: Stream Shuffle Broadcast; nki/library/api/router-topk.rst :: Bias Broadcasting

rule: For K/V longer than 10K tokens process the KV sequence in 8K-token sections (flash attention) so each section fits SBUF.
why: Full scores for very long sequences exceed on-chip memory.
trigger: Prefill attention with long context.
fix: attention_cte handles this internally; replicate in custom kernels.

rule: Software-pipeline attention across Q groups so group i does PV+writeback, group i+1 does exp, and group i+2 does Q load + QK.
why: Overlapping stages on TensorE, ScalarE and DMA keeps all engines busy.
trigger: Writing a prefill attention loop.
fix: Unroll by 3 with staggered stage assignment per Q group.

rule: Shard prefill attention across two cores primarily on batch, falling back to sequence sharding for odd batch sizes.
why: Batch sharding avoids cross-core reductions; sequence sharding balances odd batches.
trigger: attention_cte under kernel[2].
fix: Launch with a 1-D SPMD grid for LNC2.

rule: Pre-scale Q by softmax_scale on the caller side and pass scale=1.0 when using sliding window, context parallel or prefix caching in attention_cte.
why: Those modes require scale == 1.0 inside the kernel.
trigger: Ring attention / SWA / prefix caching with attention_cte.
fix: q = q * (1/sqrt(d)); attention_cte(q, k, v, scale=1.0, sliding_window=w)
check_sketch: scale!=1.0 and (sliding_window or global_cp_deg or k_prior) -> error.

rule: With causal masking skip MM1 and MM2 entirely for fully-masked upper-triangle tiles instead of computing and masking them.
why: Compute skipping halves the attention FLOPs for causal prefill.
trigger: Causal attention tile loop.
fix: if kv_tile_start > q_tile_end: continue

rule: Pass attention_cte q as (B, d, S_q) (tp_q=False, d on partitions) or (B, S_q, d) with tp_q=True for an internal DMA transpose; v is always (B_kv, S_kv, d); d <= 128.
why: QK^T contracts on d; PV contracts on S_kv so V keeps S on partitions.
trigger: Prefill attention inputs.
fix: attention_cte(q=[B,d,S], k=[B,d,S], v=[B,S,d], tp_q=False, tp_k=False)

rule: When a caller (e.g. ring attention) will merge partial softmax results, request unnormalized output plus raw denominators (skip_output_normalization=True with cache_softmax=True) and normalize once at the end.
why: Avoids repeated 1/S normalization per step.
trigger: Context-parallel attention across ranks.
fix: attention_cte(..., cache_softmax=True, skip_output_normalization=True)

rule: Note that attention_mxfp8_tkg (trn3) puts q_heads H on the partition axis for packed-Q eviction, unlike attention_tkg which puts d on partitions; it requires q_head == 64, d_head == 128 and bucket >= 2048 tokens.
why: Packed-Q eviction and the [num_blocks,32,160] MXFP8 KV block format dictate the layout.
trigger: Choosing the MXFP8 decode attention.
fix: q=[B,64,1,128] bf16; k_prior/v_prior [num_blocks,32,160] fp32 (128 tokens per block); mask [B*num_chunks,128,score_free] uint8.

rule: Pad block tables with -1 to make the kernel skip DMA for missing blocks, and prepend -1 padding when the last prior segment is shorter than prior_seg_size.
why: block_tables entries of -1 trigger DMA skipping in attention_segmented_cte.
trigger: Paged KV prefill with partial segments.
fix: block_tables[b, :pad] = -1; prior_tokens multiple of block_size.

rule: With FP8 KV caches apply the K dequant scale to Q before QK^T and the V scale to the output after PV normalization instead of dequantizing the whole cache.
why: Scaling the small operand (Q or output) is far cheaper than rescaling every cached token.
trigger: k_scale/v_scale per-head-dim [128,1].
fix: attention_segmented_cte(..., k_scale=ks, v_scale=vs)

rule: Store an FP8 K cache packed as (..., block_size//2, d_head, 2) so two consecutive tokens form one bf16-width element and the cache can be DMA'd as bf16; keep V unpacked token-major.
why: DMA and views work in 16-bit widths; packing avoids a dtype cast on the K path while V is loaded as fp8 and dequantized.
trigger: FP8 KV cache in a fused SWA block.
fix: k_cache shape (num_blocks, kv_heads, block_size//2, d_head, 2) fp8 viewed as bf16.

rule: Collapse all leading dims into one outer dim ([B,S,H] -> [B*S, H]) and tile it by 128 so every partition processes one token's H vector.
why: Row-wise ops only touch the processing (minor) dim; full-partition tiles use every engine lane.
trigger: RMSNorm / quantization / row-wise kernels.
fix: outer = B*S; for t in range(ceil(outer/128)): tile=[128, H]
source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Input Tensor Outer Dimension Collapse; Tiling

rule: Tile the hidden dim in 512-element chunks when gamma is broadcast via a TensorE matmul, matching gemm_moving_fmax so each chunk fills a PSUM bank and pipelines ScalarE (scale), TensorE (gamma broadcast) and VectorE (apply).
why: 512 is the TensorE moving free-dim limit; splitting the work across three engines gives pipeline parallelism.
trigger: RMSNorm with learned gamma.
fix: for h in range(H//512): gamma_bc = matmul(ones[1,128].T, gamma[1, h*512:(h+1)*512]) in PSUM; scalar_tensor_tensor(x_chunk, inv_rms, gamma_bc)

rule: Compute sum(x^2) with nisa.activation_reduce (square + reduce-add in one ScalarE instruction) rather than a square followed by a separate reduce.
why: The reduce-add comes for free with the activation.
trigger: RMSNorm, L2 norm, variance.
fix: nisa.activation_reduce(op=nl.square, data=x, reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_res=ss)
check_sketch: activation(square) followed by tensor_reduce(add) on same tile -> fuse.

rule: Use the stack allocator (SbufManager) for kernels so SBUF/PSUM placement is deterministic within the kernel; the default allocator considers scope outside the kernel and can vary performance.
why: Deterministic addresses avoid run-to-run layout changes and fragmentation.
trigger: Any hand-tuned library-style kernel.
fix: sbm = SbufManager(0, nl.tile_size.total_available_sbuf_size); sbm.open_scope(); t = sbm.alloc_stack(shape, dtype); sbm.close_scope()

rule: Replicate the PSUM allocation of a pipelined loop across all hardware PSUM banks with directives=ncc.multi_buffer(num_hw_psum_banks) so consecutive iterations write different banks.
why: Separate banks let TensorE write iteration i+1 while VectorE reads iteration i.
trigger: Loop issuing a matmul per iteration whose result is consumed by another engine.
fix: for i in nl.affine_range(n, directives=ncc.multi_buffer(constants.num_hw_psum_banks)): ...

rule: Disable the compiler's heuristic middle-end loop reordering/fusion (skip_middle_end_transformations) for hand-tuned kernels whose loop structure is deliberate.
why: Those passes are unpredictable and can undo manual tiling decisions.
trigger: Performance varies unexpectedly after compiler changes.
fix: Set the skip_middle_end_transformations directive on the kernel.

rule: Leave matmul results in PSUM and consume them directly (e.g. scalar_tensor_tensor reading PSUM) when the consumer is pipelined with TensorE; early eviction to SBUF buys little.
why: VectorE/ScalarE can read PSUM; an extra copy only adds work when the pipeline is already balanced.
trigger: Gamma-broadcast result waiting on inverse-RMS scale.
fix: Split work into part 1 (fill banks) and part 2 (pipelined consume) instead of evicting.

rule: Expect the compiler to split a [1,H] load into many tiny (e.g. 4-byte) DMAs because of trivial-dimension optimizations; reshape small vectors onto more partitions when this shows in the profile.
why: Trivial dims defeat descriptor coalescing.
trigger: Gamma/bias load appears as many 4 B DMAs.
fix: Load gamma as [128, H/128] or broadcast via TensorE once.

rule: Expect the abs-max -> scale -> clamp -> reciprocal -> multiply quantization chain to run serially on VectorE; overlap it with another tile's work rather than trying to parallelize within one tile.
why: Each step depends on the previous result.
trigger: FP8 row quantization.
fix: Process tiles in batches of 8 so independent chains interleave.
source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Phase 3: Quantization; nki/library/api/rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Optimized Batch Processing

rule: Pack per-row dequant scales into the tail of the quantized output row ([..., H+4] fp8 reinterpreted as fp32) so one tensor carries data and scales.
why: Neuron cannot pack two dtypes in one tensor natively; appending 4 fp8 bytes per row lets collectives/gathers move both at once.
trigger: Sequence-parallel RMSNorm-quant followed by all-gather.
fix: out[..., :H] = fp8 data; out[..., H:H+4] = fp32 scale bits.

rule: Allocate long-lived buffers (weights) with alloc_heap at the top of SBUF and release them with pop_heap in LIFO order; allocate temporaries with alloc_stack inside open_scope/close_scope so they free automatically.
why: The stack grows up from the lower bound and the heap down from the upper bound; close_scope resets the stack pointer so sibling scopes reuse memory.
trigger: Multi-phase kernels with different temporaries per phase.
fix: w=sbm.alloc_heap((128,256), nl.bfloat16); sbm.open_scope('phase'); t=sbm.alloc_stack(...); sbm.close_scope(); sbm.pop_heap()
check_sketch: Every open_scope has matching close_scope; alloc_heap count == pop_heap count.

rule: Double/triple buffer loop temporaries with open_scope(interleave_degree=N) and increment_section() each iteration so loads of iteration i+1 land in a different section than compute of iteration i.
why: Allocations rotate through N address sections (e.g. 0, 1024, 0, 1024), letting DMA and compute overlap.
trigger: Pipelined tile loop.
fix: sbm.open_scope(interleave_degree=2); for i in range(N): buf=sbm.alloc_stack((128,512), nl.bfloat16); ...; sbm.increment_section(); sbm.close_scope()

rule: When permuting a TensorView of an SBUF tensor keep dim 0 at position 0, use reshape_dim instead of general reshape (unimplemented), and check has_dynamic_access() before further slicing.
why: Views cannot move data across partitions; reshape is only implemented per dimension.
trigger: Reinterpreting [128, S, 3*H*D] QKV in SBUF as heads.
fix: TensorView(qkv).reshape_dim(2,(3,H,D)).select(2,0).permute((0,2,1,3)).get_view()
check_sketch: permute dims[0]!=0 on sbuf -> error.

rule: In a multi-layer decode megakernel keep the residual stream in SBUF and use SBUF-to-SBUF all-reduce (sbuf_residual_and_cc=True) instead of round-tripping through HBM each layer.
why: transformer_tkg runs attention -> all-reduce -> MLP -> all-reduce per layer; SBUF residual removes HBM traffic and launch overhead.
trigger: Token-generation transformer with TP all-reduces.
fix: transformer_tkg(..., sbuf_residual_and_cc=True, replica_groups=...)

rule: Fuse multiple transformer layers into one kernel invocation for decode to cut kernel launch overhead and enable cross-layer prefetch.
why: Per-kernel NEFF start-up/tear-down dominates when each layer's compute is tiny.
trigger: Decode with many small layers.
fix: transformer_tkg(X, W_qkvs, W_outs, W_gates, W_ups, W_downs, ..., num_layers=L)

rule: Use moe_tkg when T = batch*seq <= 128 (except MX all-expert mode) and moe_cte with blockwise matmul when T > 128.
why: TKG processes all tokens on one partition tile; CTE groups tokens into expert blocks.
trigger: MoE layer in decode vs prefill.
fix: moe_tkg(hidden[T,H] or SBUF [H0,T,H1], ..., output_in_sbuf=True)

rule: Feed moe_tkg SBUF inputs as [H0=128, T, H1=H/128] (hidden split across partitions) and prefer POST_SCALE affinity mode; I_p = I//4 if I <= 512 else 128 for MX weights.
why: The TKG kernel contracts over H by iterating H1 tiles with 128 on partitions.
trigger: Fusing norm/router output into the MoE kernel.
fix: moe_tkg(hidden_input=sbuf_tile[128,T,H//128], expert_affinities_scaling_mode=POST_SCALE)

rule: For moe_cte use block_size 256-1024 (multiple of 256), H 512-8192 (multiple of 512, optimal 2048-4096), I_TP 2048-16384 (divisible by 16, optimal 8192), E 8-64, T <= 32K, int32 routing tensors.
why: Validated ranges of the blockwise kernels.
trigger: Prefill MoE.
fix: moe_cte(..., block_size=512, spec=MoECTESpec(implementation=shard_on_block))

rule: Shard MoE prefill on blocks (shard_on_block, PING_PONG/HI_LO) when there are many blocks; shard the intermediate dimension (shard_on_i) otherwise, accepting an all-reduce to combine partials; use the _mx variants on trn3.
why: Block sharding has no cross-core reduction but needs enough blocks to balance; I-sharding always balances but reduces.
trigger: LNC2 MoE CTE.
fix: MoECTESpec(implementation=MoECTEImplementation.shard_on_block)  # or shard_on_i / shard_on_i_hybrid

rule: Process the compile-time-known non-padded blocks in a static (unrolled) loop and the variable padded tail in a dynamic loop with early exit, driven by a conditions vector whose last entry is 0.
why: Static loops get full scheduling; the dynamic tail avoids wasted work on padded blocks.
trigger: MoE blockwise matmul with padded block counts.
fix: bwmm_shard_on_block_hybrid(conditions=[1,1,...,0], num_static_block=N-E, ...)

rule: When token routing guarantees shards never touch the same output rows (e.g. HI_LO with sequence sharding), set non_overlapping_shards=True to skip zero-init and the cross-shard reduce.
why: The accumulation output [T,2,H+E] and its FMA reduce exist only to merge overlapping shard writes.
trigger: Blockwise MoE with disjoint token sets per core.
fix: bwmm_shard_on_block(..., block_sharding_strategy=HI_LO, non_overlapping_shards=True)

rule: Load per-expert weight slices with a scalar_offset taken from a (1,1) SBUF expert-index tile instead of unrolling over experts.
why: Dynamic indexing on the DMA lets one code path serve any expert; partial tiles are zero-padded.
trigger: block_to_expert-driven weight loads.
fix: load_gate_up_proj_weights(gate_up_proj_weight[E,H,2,I_TP], block_expert_sb[1,1], ...)

rule: Keep router top-K with K <= 8, E <= 512 (gemm_moving_fmax), H multiple of 128; SIGMOID and router_pre_norm require use_indirect_dma_scatter, which needs T <= 128 or a multiple of 128; SBUF output needs T <= 128.
why: Top-K uses max8/nc_find_index8 (8 per instruction) and the logits matmul puts E on the moving free dim.
trigger: MoE router.
fix: router_topk(x, w, bias, ..., k=8, use_indirect_dma_scatter=True)

rule: For matmuls with very few tokens (T < 128) split the PE array column-wise into 32/64/128-column tiles so several independent matmuls run in parallel instead of under-filling the array.
why: A decode matmul with T rows uses only T of 128 columns; column tiling recovers utilization.
trigger: Router logits or projections in decode.
fix: router_topk(..., use_column_tiling=True); mlp(use_tkg_*_column_tiling=True)
source: nki/library/api/router-topk.rst :: PE Array Column Tiling; nki/library/api/mlp.rst

rule: For tiny decode kernels (T <= 128) let both cores compute identical results and shard only the HBM store across cores for bandwidth.
why: Compute is negligible; splitting the store halves per-core write traffic without any inter-core exchange.
trigger: Fused RMSNorm + router for MoE token generation.
fix: rmsnorm_router_topk_a2av: both NCs compute, store sharded.

rule: rmsnorm_router_topk_tkg requires LNC=2; with no quantization H must be divisible by 128 and T a multiple of 256 (DLoC tiling); with MX quantization H must be divisible by 512.
why: Library constraints tied to the sharding and MX block size.
trigger: Fused norm+router in MoE decode.
fix: kernel[2](...) with T%256==0.

rule: When a matmul consumes swizzle-transposed MX activations, pre-permute the weight rows offline into swizzle order h_swz = h512*512 + 4*p + q (p = partition 0..127, q = lane 0..3) and leave hidden states/gamma in natural order.
why: The FP32-packed transpose used by quantize_mx places hidden index h at swizzled partition slot; weights must match or logits are wrong.
trigger: rmsnorm_mx_prefill with router_weights; any nc_matmul_mx on swizzled activations.
fix: W_perm = W[swizzle_h_index(H)] where swizzle_h_index returns (h512*512 + 4*p + q).reshape(-1).

rule: Keep pack_scales=True so four H512 tiles of MX scales fold into one 128-wide block (scale region ~H/16 columns) instead of H/4 with 7/8 padding.
why: quantize_mx emits one uint8 scale per (32-partition quadrant x 4 lanes), occupying 4 of every 32 columns after transpose.
trigger: Packed MX output rows.
fix: rmsnorm_mx_prefill(..., pack_scales=True)

rule: When H is zero-padded to a multiple of 512, pass unpadded_hidden_size so the RMS mean divides by the true H while the sum of squares runs over the padded H.
why: Zero padding contributes 0 to the sum but would wrongly enlarge the denominator.
trigger: Padded hidden dims for MX block alignment.
fix: rmsnorm_mx_prefill(..., unpadded_hidden_size=H_true)

rule: Treat MXFP8 operands as 4-packed: a physical [128,128] LHS tile is a logical [512,128] (K=512 per tile), RHS physical [128,512] is logical [512,512]; keep K divisible by 512 and swizzle to [K/4, M*4].
why: float8_e4m3fn_x4 packs four K elements per partition entry.
trigger: matmul_mxfp8 / nc_matmul_mx.
fix: quantize_block_mxfp8_kernel(src[F,K]) -> scales [K//4, F], data [K//4, F*4]; LNC2 needs >= 2 blocks in N.

rule: Keep activations in BF16 (not pre-quantized MXFP8) when they are gathered per block via indirect DMA, because row gathers break the 32-element MX quantization group alignment.
why: MX scales are shared by 32 consecutive elements; gathering rows scrambles the groups.
trigger: Blockwise MoE forward/backward with MXFP8 weights.
fix: blockwise_mm_fwd_mxfp8(hidden_states bf16, gate_up_proj_weight MXFP8 + scales)

rule: Choose the vocabulary chunk for online-LSE cross entropy as V for V <= 32K, 32768/40960 for 32K-128K, 65535 (bf16) or 32768 (fp32) for 128K-256K, and keep positions_per_batch x chunk_size x dtype_bytes <= 24 MiB.
why: Chunks must fit SBUF (24 MiB budget) and the free-dim hardware limit (65535) while minimizing loop iterations.
trigger: Large-vocab loss kernel.
fix: cross_entropy_forward(logits, targets, positions_per_batch=32, chunk_size=32768)
check_sketch: ppb*chunk*bytes <= 24 MiB and chunk <= min(V, 65535).

rule: Implement row gathers (input[index]) with an indirect DMA load whose offsets come from the index tensor; under LNC sharding make the index count divisible by the shard count.
why: DMA engines support scatter/gather natively, avoiding per-row loops.
trigger: Embedding lookup, token permutation.
fix: gather(input[N,D], dim=0, index[K])  # K % num_shards == 0

rule: Ensure indices within each 128-row tile are unique when using the gather-accumulate-scatter pattern; duplicate indices in a tile lose updates.
why: The pattern reads old rows, adds, and writes back once per tile with no atomicity.
trigger: scatter_add with repeated targets.
fix: Pre-sort/deduplicate indices or use the accumulating MoE unpermute path.
check_sketch: Duplicate indices within any 128-chunk -> warn.

rule: Use the out-of-bounds sentinel (index == T) with oob_mode.skip so unused slots in a fixed-size indirect DMA index become no-ops.
why: Fixed-shape index tensors need a way to express variable counts without branching.
trigger: all-to-all-v dispatch/combine with per-destination counts.
fix: send_indices[t, d] = T for slots beyond send_counts[d].

rule: Run per-partition free-dim sorting ops (max8, nc_match_replace8, nc_n_gather) once across up to 128 partitions instead of once per 8-row tile; the extra partitions are free VectorE parallelism.
why: These instructions operate per partition along the free dim, so widening costs nothing and removes redundant passes that were the measured bottleneck.
trigger: Sorting K candidates per row after topk.
fix: Phase 1: topk per 8-row tile -> HBM; phase 2: one sort over 128 rows.

rule: Accumulate cumsum/linear scans in fp32 regardless of input dtype, tile the free dim at 2048 and carry the last column into the next tile's initial value; expect ~1e-2 abs error beyond ~5K elements.
why: tensor_tensor_scan precision degrades over long sequences; fp32 limits drift.
trigger: Long cumulative sums.
fix: cumsum(x) / linear_scan(decay, data, initial)

rule: Accumulate across the state dimension in SBUF per free tile rather than read-modify-write to HBM (which needs trn2 shared memory); store carries in the final_state HBM tensor.
why: HBM RMW is slow and generation-dependent; SBUF accumulation is local.
trigger: Mamba selective scan over state_size.
fix: selective_scan with F tile 512; channels on partitions (128).

rule: Overlap collectives with compute by ring-based collective_permute with double buffering (fine_grained_allgather / allgather_compute_matmul), choosing the SBUF path when the tensor fits and HBM otherwise.
why: Fine-grained ring steps let matmul on chunk i proceed while chunk i+1 is in flight.
trigger: TP all-gather followed by matmul.
fix: allgather_compute_matmul(lhs[m,K], rhs[K,N], tp_degree=8, num_groups=1)  # trn2, tp_degree even, M % (RANK_N*LNC_N*CHANNEL_N)==0

rule: Use allgather_sb2sb only when H*W*dtype fits SBUF with H <= 128 partitions; otherwise use allgather_sb2sb_tiled (TILE_M capped at 128, tiles distributed over LNC cores).
why: SBUF-to-SBUF collectives avoid HBM but need the whole tensor on-chip.
trigger: Gathering small activations across TP ranks.
fix: allgather_sb2sb_tiled(inp[M,K], replica_groups, tp_degree) -> [M, K*tp]

rule: Precompute per-rank offsets in a lookup tensor (iota_workers) and read it with rank_id as scalar_offset, because the NKI compiler does not support arithmetic on rank_id.
why: rank_id is a runtime register value; a table converts it into any derived offset.
trigger: Rank-dependent slicing after an all_gather.
fix: iota=[(r % G)*B_per_rank for r in ranks]; offset = dma(iota, scalar_offset=rank_id)

rule: Derive dimensions like H from tensor shapes inside the kernel; do not pass them as runtime scalars, because the framework materializes them as HBM tensors and shape math built on them is garbage.
why: Only trace-time Python ints participate in specialization.
trigger: Kernel signature with an int that the framework wraps as a tensor.
fix: H = wuv_qtz_hbm.shape[0]*4 // L  instead of a runtime H argument.
check_sketch: int-typed kernel arg used in shape arithmetic that is actually a tensor at trace time -> error.

rule: When splitting a fused op into two kernels, write the intermediate in the layout the consumer's DMA-transpose expects (e.g. MX 4-pack column order) so the consumer gets a contiguous swdge dma_transpose off TensorE.
why: Pre-permuting columns in the producer turns an expensive gather in the consumer into a contiguous DMA.
trigger: Split MLA sparse attention -> V-up/o-proj.
fix: Producer writes column sub*(L//4)+group for latent l=4*group+sub; keep producer, consumer loads and refs in lockstep.

rule: Keep projections in MX but compute attention scores with bf16 nc_matmul so the Q swizzle + quantize_mx + Hadamard chain leaves the per-tile critical path; Hadamard rotation is a mathematical no-op (q H H^T k^T = q k^T).
why: The rotation only exists to make MX quantization well-behaved; without score quantization it is unnecessary and precision improves.
trigger: Sparse-attention indexer or any score path with MX inputs.
fix: sparse_attention_indexer_mx_bf16score(...)

rule: For ring attention keep per-rank sequence length divisible by 128, broadcast KV heads to match Q heads (MHA only), pre-scale Q when causal, and expect LSE as [b,h,128,S//128].
why: Attention tiles are 128 on partitions and the kernel requires trn2+.
trigger: Context-parallel training attention.
fix: ring_attention_spmd_fwd(q,k,v, replica_groups, num_workers, softmax_scale=1.0, use_causal_mask=True)
